subject: KMS/HSM options, logging & retention — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medlytics.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood KMS/HSM options for MedLytics PII workload

Thanks again for the quick demo this morning — good context. As we discussed on the call, MedLytics needs to document the encryption and logging controls we'll require before moving the pilot into an exec review. High-level asks: 1) support for customer-managed keys (BYOK) with the option to use our HSM-backed key material, 2) confirmation of in-transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) and at-rest encryption, 3) sample audit log lines showing key usage (encrypt/decrypt/rotate) and request/response traces, 4) retention controls for request logs and raw input (we aim for 90-day retention for raw inputs, longer for anonymized metrics), and 5) a short runbook describing how CMK integration works end-to-end (KMS calls, envelope encryption, key rotation, emergency key revoke).

I'm attaching our internal requirements doc (MedLytics-data-handling-requirements.pdf). Can you send a concise summary and an estimated timeline to get BYOK + HSM wrap enabled for a POC? Also let us know what SOC 2 artifacts you can share now.

Laura Chen
Head of Security & Privacy
MedLytics, Inc.

Attachment: MedLytics-data-handling-requirements.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medlytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood KMS/HSM options for MedLytics PII workload

Hi Laura — thanks for laying that out and for sharing the doc. Follow-up notes below and attached a short summary that maps to each of your asks (redwood-kms-hsm-options-summary.pdf). TL;DR: we support BYOK via all major cloud CMEK integrations and have an HSM-wrap option for customers requiring FIPS 140-2 level HSM separation.

Answers to your numbered list:
1) BYOK/HSM: Redwood can integrate with AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and Azure Key Vault for envelope encryption. For HSM-backed keys, we offer two approaches: (a) cloud-managed HSM (CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM) where the master key never leaves the HSM and we call the KMS to wrap/unwrap, or (b) customer-supplied external HSM that performs wrapping for a locally managed key (we support PKCS#11 and KMIP-based workflows). We can demonstrate a PKCS#11 wrap POC.

2) In-transit & At-rest: All customer API traffic is TLS 1.3 (fallback to TLS 1.2 disabled by default). At-rest data is encrypted using AES-256 with envelope encryption keyed by the CMK. Keys used for tokenization/KV caches are similarly wrapped.

3) Audit logs: We can provide structured key-usage events (JSON lines) that include: timestamp, operation (Encrypt/Decrypt/Rotate), key_id (obfuscated), request_id, consumer_identity, and result code. We can redact sensitive prompt text from logs; by default raw prompt text is not stored in long-term index unless explicitly enabled. Sample log snippets available in the attached summary.

4) Retention: Platform defaults to 30 days for raw request payloads and 365 days for operational logs. For enterprise customers we offer configurable retention policies (30/90/365/never delete) and can enforce a maximum retention window. We can support your 90-day raw-input retention requirement for the pilot.

5) Runbook & artifacts: Attached is our high-level runbook and a checklist for integrating CMK (redwood-kms-hsm-options-summary.pdf). We can also share SOC 2 Type II cover letter and the compliance pack under an NDA.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep dive (1-hour) with your infra/security engineers to walk through PKCS#11 wrap flow and logging schema (target week of 3/8)
- POC plan for BYOK + HSM wrap (2-3 weeks by our infra team once we have a test key)
- Exchange of minimal legal / technical documents (we'll review any required T&C/KMS language)

I've included Marissa to coordinate the commercial / timeline side. If that sounds good, I'll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive and include our security engineer (Karthik) for the PKCS#11 discussion.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood-kms-hsm-options-summary.pdf

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medlytics.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood KMS/HSM options for MedLytics PII workload

Thanks, Soojin — that is helpful. Quick clarifications before the deep-dive:
- Rotation cadence: MedLytics policy requires cryptographic key rotation every 90 days for keys that encrypt PII. Can Redwood enforce automated rotation and provide rotation events in the audit stream?
- Key custodianship: We need proof that key material can be restricted to our HSM and that Redwood personnel cannot perform raw key extract operations. Do you have a PKCS#11 / HSM architecture diagram for the external-HSM option?
- Logs: please include an example of a log line that shows an AES envelope unwrap for a request_id but does not contain the request payload.
- Data retention: confirm that raw prompt text will not be retained beyond the retention window and describe the deletion process (soft-delete vs immediate purge).

Attaching the legal KMS clauses for our team (medlytics-legal-KMS-clauses.docx) — please review. We'd also like your SOC 2 summary (or the compliance pack under NDA) ahead of the exec call.

Laura Chen
Head of Security & Privacy
MedLytics, Inc.

Attachment: medlytics-legal-KMS-clauses.docx
